evidence_items.locator: Capital Investments, page 77; Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows, page 91
evidence_items.explanation: The cash-flow statement gives $10.309 billion of cash capital expenditure and $3.058 billion of operating cash inflow, implying $7.251 billion of net burn under the standard subtraction. This would contradict $15 billion under that definition, but the estimate's matching basis has not been established.

metric_scope.metric: Calculated cash capital expenditure less operating cash flow

inputs: 2025 cash purchases of property and equipment, including capitalized internal-use software: USD 10,309 million
2025 net cash provided by operating activities: USD 3,058 million
derived.formula: (10,309 - 3,058) / 1,000 = USD 7.251 billion of net cash burn
derived.rounding: Exact to the reported million; approximately USD 7.3 billion. Inputs are audited; this subtraction is an evaluator calculation.

evidence_items.locator: CFO discussion of capital expenditures and construction in progress
evidence_items.explanation: Management reports $14.9 billion of full-year capital expenditures in a discussion tied to infrastructure deployment. Its numerical proximity to $15 billion cannot support a net cash-burn forecast: it is a different, gross investment measure.
